extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement for modifier 62.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to professional services only. In some situations, it is necessary for two surgeons to work together, each as a primary surgeon, on the same patient during the same operative session due to factors such as the complexity of the procedure or the condition of the patient. This can include surgeries when two surgeons of different specialties are required for a specific procedure. This can also include surgeries in which two surgeons perform elements of the procedure simultaneously such as during bilateral knee replacement or a heart transplant. In such circumstances, the physicians are considered co-surgeons, not assistant surgeons. Note: Surgeons of different specialties performing distinct procedures, even if the procedures use the same incision site, are not considered co-surgeons. Humana requires each surgeon acting as a co-surgeon to append modifier 62 to a procedure code with a Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File co-surgeon indicator 1 or 2.

extracted_content.title: Co-surgeon Indicator 1
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Co-surgeon Indicator 1
extracted_content.content: Humana may allow the services of co-surgeons for a procedure with an MPFS Relative Value File co-surgeon indicator 1, if Humana determines it was medically necessary for more than one surgeon to perform the procedure. Medical necessity of the co-surgeon services must be documented in the medical record, and the claim may be subject to records review. If Humana determines the services of co-surgeons are medically necessary in that situation, then the amount allowed for each surgeon's charge is determined as noted in the section above regarding procedures with an MPFS Relative Value File co-surgeon indicator 2. If Humana determines the services of co-surgeons are not medically necessary in that situation, then co-surgeon charges will be processed as noted in the section above regarding procedures with an MPFS Relative Value File co-surgeon indicator 0.

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to professional services only. In some situations, it is necessary for two surgeons to work together, each as a primary surgeon, on the same patient during the same operative session due to factors such as the complexity of the procedure or the condition of the patient. This can include surgeries when two surgeons of different specialties are required for a specific procedure. This can also include surgeries in which two surgeons perform elements of the procedure simultaneously such as during bilateral knee replacement or a heart transplant. In such circumstances, the physicians are considered co-surgeons, not assistant surgeons. Note: Surgeons of different specialties performing distinct procedures, even if the procedures use the same incision site, are not considered co-surgeons. Humana requires each surgeon acting as a co-surgeon to append modifier 62 to a procedure code with a Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File co-surgeon indicator 1 or 2.

Humana allows the services of co-surgeons for a procedure with an MPFS Relative Value File co-surgeon indicator 2, when the surgeons determine it is necessary for more than one surgeon to perform the procedure. In these situations, each surgeon submits a charge with modifier 62. The amount allowed for each surgeon's charge is the lesser of the following:

The billed charge amount;

62.5 percent of the surgeon's contracted rate; or

62.5 percent of the base maximum amount payable under the member's plan, for an out-of-network surgeon. In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply. For example, when applicable, multiple surgery reduction is applied after a co-surgeon reduction.

Humana does not allow the services of co-surgeons for a procedure with an MPFS Relative Value File co-surgeon indicator 0. If a charge for such a service is submitted with modifier 62, Humana denies the charge.

Humana may allow the services of co-surgeons for a procedure with an MPFS Relative Value File co-surgeon indicator 1, if Humana determines it was medically necessary for more than one surgeon to perform the procedure. Medical necessity of the co-surgeon services must be documented in the medical record, and the claim may be subject to records review. If Humana determines the services of co-surgeons are medically necessary in that situation, then the amount allowed for each surgeon's charge is determined as noted in the section above regarding procedures with an MPFS Relative Value File co-surgeon indicator 2. If Humana determines the services of co-surgeons are not medically necessary in that situation, then co-surgeon charges will be processed as noted in the section above regarding procedures with an MPFS Relative Value File co-surgeon indicator 0.

Base maximum amount payable under the member's plan: The maximum amount of reimbursement for a covered expense, determined by the member's plan. Depending on the plan, this may be the maximum allowable fee, the appropriate Medicare fee schedule rate or an amount derived from another payment model. Actual plan reimbursement may be less than this base maximum amount, because of applicable adjustments.

Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File: A file published by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services that includes, among other information, co-surgeon indicator, relative value units and conversion factors for physician services. This file is commonly referred to as the relative value unit (RVU) table.

Modifier 62: Two surgeons.
